m1-red.title: TDD red: write test_sector_nesting.py for nest_sectors (exactness, split-not-snap, sliver-exempt, fail-closed, completeness, sector assignment)
m1-red.imperative: Create tests/unit/physics/segment_map/derivation/test_sector_nesting.py with hand-built synthetic tilings (deterministic boundaries_m/seg_type_code arrays, no ReferenceLap needed) covering each nest_sectors rule as its OWN test: (1) exactness -- every sector line distance appears as an exact output boundary; (2) split-not-snap -- a segment straddling a sector line splits into TWO pieces of the SAME seg_type at the line's EXACT distance, verified against a fixture where the nearest pre-existing boundary is NOT the line (so snapping would produce a visibly different, wrong result); (3) sliver-merge exempts sector cuts -- a synthetic <MIN_SEGMENT_LENGTH_M sliver away from any sector line merges into a neighbor, AND a separate fixture where a <MIN_SEGMENT_LENGTH_M sliver's boundary IS a sector line and that boundary survives (is NOT removed); (4) fail-closed -- SectorLineUnavailableError raised for a line outside (0, lap_length_m), a NaN line, and an unplaceable case (e.g. two lines not strictly increasing, or wrong count); (5) completeness preserved -- after nesting, an independent recomputation confirms boundaries_m strictly increasing, [0]==0.0, [-1]==lap_length_m, no gaps/overlaps; (6) sector int8 assignment -- each output segment's sector (1/2/3) matches which FIA interval its midpoint falls in, verified on a fixture spanning all three sectors. Import MIN_SEGMENT_LENGTH_M from src.physics.layer2.frozen_constants in the test file itself (never hardcode 5.0). Run the test file on the pinned interpreter and observe it fail (module sector_nesting.py does not exist yet). Attest c1 (manual, do NOT run as a command check).
